discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, and LMU Munich, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Zoller showed theoretically that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with fully tunable parameters, turning Feynman's idea of a quantum simulator into a concrete laboratory program. Bloch and Greiner then observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition (2002), the first clean realization of a strongly correlated many-body phase in a synthetic quantum system. Their subsequent development of quantum gas microscopes, with single-site resolution and control, enabled direct imaging of antiferromagnetic order, many-body localization, entanglement entropy and non-equilibrium dynamics beyond classical computation. Together these contributions founded analog quantum simulation as a new field of physics, bridging quantum optics, condensed matter and quantum information, and now underpin neutral-atom quantum computing platforms worldwide.
